title: The Salt Compass
premise: Tamsin Okafor, a salvage diver haunted by her father's debts and the brass compass he left her, is diving an uncharted wreck off the West African coast when a government survey team vanishes without a trace. The compass, she learns, is not a keepsake but a key—one of two instruments that locate the Meridian, a colonial-era vessel carrying a fortune in gold and a ledger naming every family enriched by the slave trade, including her own. Racing the salvage fleet and the monsoon across six tides, Tamsin must decide whether to sell the truth or set it free. In the end she scuttles the wreck's treasure into protected deep water, publishes the ledger, and claims her identity not as an heir to stolen wealth but as the woman who returned it.
about_author: C. M. Oyelaran is a former marine cartographer who spent five years charting wrecks along the Gulf of Guinea before turning to fiction. Their work draws on oral histories gathered in coastal fishing towns, blending archival research with salt-stained adventure.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Tamsin dives a navy-restricted wreck at dawn, salvaging a corroded strongbox while her boat's engine dies and her debt collector radios threats. Her POV establishes her precarity, skill, and stubborn independence. Emotional beat: weary defiance—she owns almost nothing, but the sea answers to her.

chapters.title: The Brass Needle
chapters.summary: Cleaning the strongbox at her dockside shack, Tamsin finds inside it a second compass identical to her father's, its needle pointing not north but seaward. Flashbacks reveal her father's drowning and his whispered warnings about 'the Meridian.' Emotional beat: unease—the past has been waiting underwater.

chapters.title: Gear With No Tracks
chapters.summary: A government survey team's abandoned camp appears on a nearby cay: generators still warm, meals half-eaten, no footprints leading out. Tamsin, first on scene, pockets a waterlogged logbook before officials arrive. Emotional beat: creeping dread—invisibility was always her armor, and it's failing.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Shadow
chapters.summary: In the logbook, coordinates match her compasses' crossing point. A naval officer, Commander Reyes, interrogates her and lets slip that the survey team found 'documents better left drowned.' Tamsin realizes the navy wants the wreck silent. Emotional beat: cold clarity about how power protects itself.

chapters.title: Debt of Salt
chapters.summary: Her creditor, salvage magnate Eze Boateng, offers to clear her debt if she hands over anything she recovers from the restricted zone. She signs nothing but says enough for him to smell profit. His POV shows a man who converts everything—including people—into assets. Emotional beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: What Papa Buried
chapters.summary: Tamsin visits her aunt in Lagos, who reveals her father was a diver on the original 1960s search for the Meridian and stole one compass to keep it from being sold abroad. The compasses are twin keys; together they triangulate the hold. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: First Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin races out ahead of Boateng's fleet, using both compasses to fix the true site miles from the navy's charts. Diving through a storm surge, she touches the Meridian's hull and finds the survey team's marker buoy snagged on the rail. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear—someone got here first.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stayed Behind
chapters.summary: She finds Kwesi Mensah, the survey team's missing hydrographer, hiding in a sea cave—he faked the disappearance when colleagues began dying after reading the ledger. His POV delivers exposition on the gold and the names. Emotional beat: two loners choosing cautious trust.

chapters.title: Names in the Hold
chapters.summary: Together they reach the cargo hold: gold bars fused with coral, and a lead-lined chest of documents—the ledger listing merchant families, including 'Okafor,' her own line, recorded as collaborators. Tamsin's POV fractures under the revelation. Emotional beat: identity shaken at the root.

chapters.title: Second Tide
chapters.summary: Boateng's lead vessel arrives early, forcing Tamsin and Kwesi to hide among the wrecks while divers swarm the site. She watches men she knows get bent and battered by greed-driven haste. Emotional beat: fury at how power spends other people's bodies.

chapters.title: Bargain at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Caught by Boateng's enforcers, Tamsin trades the false coordinates from the navy's charts to buy their release, keeping the true location secret. Reyes observes the exchange and now knows she's holding back. Emotional beat: shame braided with resolve—she lied well and hates it.

chapters.title: The Navy's Quiet Interest
chapters.summary: Reyes detains them aboard his ship, offering official protection in exchange for the ledger—which would vanish into classified archives. He reveals the government's founding families are in it too. Tamsin stalls. Emotional beat: recognizing that every hand reaching for the truth means to bury it.

chapters.title: Third Tide
chapters.summary: Escaping Reyes's custody during a supply transfer, they steal a skiff and run for the open site as the barometer falls. Kwesi confesses he let his teammates die by staying silent too long. Emotional beat: guilt met with forgiveness neither fully believes yet.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Harbor radio confirms landfall in three tides. Boateng's fleet, tipped by a bribed harbormaster, converges on the true coordinates Tamsin's borrowed skiff inadvertently broadcast. Her POV calculates odds and finds them ugly. Emotional beat: cornered ingenuity—the diver becomes the strategist.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: A night dive in worsening swell: Tamsin raises the ledger chest alone while Kwesi rigs decoy buoys. Boateng's divers nearly catch her; she escapes by flooding a compartment and dropping through the hull breach. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce competence.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Storm winds scatter the fleet. Boateng boards Tamsin's beached skiff personally and offers her everything—debt cleared, a fleet of her own—if she surrenders the ledger. She refuses, and he takes her father's compass instead, leaving her one key and a deadline. Emotional beat: loss sharpening purpose.

chapters.title: The Weight of Gold
chapters.summary: Sheltering ashore, Tamsin reads the ledger cover to cover and drafts the choice before her: sell it, leak it, or sink it. Kwesi argues for publication; she fears becoming what her ancestors were—someone profiting from the dead. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—power corrupts even good intentions.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: The monsoon hits. In chaos, Boateng's flagship anchors directly over the wreck to raise the gold before the sea closes the window. Tamsin and Kwesi sail into the storm, using her remaining compass and his survey data to reach the site beneath the fleet's sonar shadow. Emotional beat: reckless courage against impossible weather.

chapters.title: Scuttle
chapters.summary: Climax below: Tamsin plants charges in the Meridian's weakened hull while Boateng's divers fight the surge above. The gold collapses into a protected trench beyond any salvage depth; Boateng, refusing to surface, goes down with his claim. Emotional beat: cathartic destruction—wealth returned to the deep.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ashore, Tamsin releases the ledger to journalists, historians, and the descendant communities named within it, including her own family's reckoning. Reyes chooses not to intervene, quietly resigning. Emotional beat: painful liberation—truth costs everything except itself.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Epilogue-dive: Tamsin returns to the trench one last time, leaving her father's recovered compass on the seabed beside the wreck. Kwesi waits aboard a small boat she now co-owns, debt-free. Emotional beat: peace—an inheritance finally hers to define.

chapters.title: North by Nothing
chapters.summary: Closing chapter: months later, Tamsin trains young coastal divers, teaching them to read water rather than chase treasure. A letter arrives from a historian thanking her; she pins it beside her father's old chart and sails out on a working morning. Emotional beat: quiet identity—she is no longer what she inherited, but what she chose.
